record.paper_title: SOFT PHYSICS AND INTERMITTENCY : OPEN QUESTION(S) in KRAKOW
record.original_question: Does perturbative QCD's predicted effective singularity in angular fluctuation or correlation variables produce observable angular intermittency in lepton-induced reactions when hadronization effects are minimized, or in other reaction classes?

evidence.quote: 5. "Angular intermittency". One property of intermittent fluctuations in particle physics suggested by perturbative QCD calculations is that an effective singularity may show up in the fluctuations/correlations for angular variables[12].

It would be interesting to look for such a behaviour, either in lepton-induced reactions by depressing as much as possible the effect of hadronisation[12], or by extension to all other cases, just for curiosity’s sake.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider high-energy particle production in which one studies the multiplicity distribution of final-state particles inside cells of phase space. For a phase-space variable (such as a rapidity, pseudo-rapidity, or angular coordinate) divided into M bins of equal size, the normalized factorial moments are defined by

  F_q(M) = ⟨ (1/M) Σ_{m=1}^{M} n_m(n_m-1)···(n_m-q+1) ⟩ / ⟨ (1/M) Σ_{m=1}^{M} n_m ⟩^q ,

where n_m is the number of particles in the m-th cell and ⟨·⟩ denotes an event average. The system is said to exhibit "intermittency" in the chosen variable if, as the bin size δ → 0 (equivalently M → ∞), the factorial moments follow a power-law

  F_q(M) ∝ M^{φ_q},   φ_q > 0,

reflecting a self-similar, scale-invariant fluctuation pattern with an effective singularity in the underlying density.

Perturbative QCD (double-leading-log parton-shower calculations, treating hadrons via parton–hadron duality) predicts that such an effective singularity, and hence intermittent power-law scaling, should appear when the cells are defined in terms of angular variables (e.g. the polar angle relative to the jet axis, or relative opening angles of particle pairs), giving rise to "angular intermittency" with computable indices φ_q that depend on the running coupling and the opening angle of the jet.

Question: In real collision data, does this predicted angular intermittency actually manifest itself as observable power-law scaling of the angular factorial moments F_q(M)? Specifically:

(a) In lepton-induced reactions (e.g. e⁺e⁻ annihilation into hadrons, or deep-inelastic lepton–nucleon scattering), where the perturbative parton-cascade contribution can be isolated by minimizing the influence of nonperturbative hadronization, do the angular factorial moments exhibit the predicted intermittent scaling with the QCD-predicted indices?

(b) Does analogous angular intermittency, qualitatively or quantitatively consistent with the perturbative prediction, occur in other classes of high-energy reactions (hadron–hadron and nucleus–nucleus collisions)?
artifact.status_search_result: Perturbative QCD predictions for angular intermittency (self-similar power-law factorial moments in angular variables) were derived analytically at double-leading-log accuracy, with parameter-free predictions for Z⁰ hadronic decays under parton-hadron duality. Subsequent experimental analyses (e+e- at LEP, and hadronic/nuclear collisions) have observed intermittency-like scaling in angular and other variables, with broad qualitative agreement with QCD parton-shower expectations, although quantitative matching to the predicted indices and full separation from hadronization effects remain incomplete. The question is therefore partially addressed rather than definitively settled.

status_evidence.title: Angular Intermittency in QCD Jets
status_evidence.snippet: Analytical formula for factorial moments in a QCD jet at DLL accuracy gives self-similar dependence on solid-angle cell size, characteristic of angular intermittency; parameter-free prediction for Z0 hadronic decays under parton-hadron duality.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical pQCD prediction for angular intermittency with explicit indices is established.

status_evidence.title: Generalised factorial moments and QCD jets
status_evidence.snippet: Generalised factorial moments computed in pQCD jets, predicting angular intermittency patterns observable in jets.
status_evidence.claim: Further perturbative-QCD predictions extending angular intermittency exist but full experimental confirmation in lepton-induced reactions is not declared.

status_evidence.title: Scaling for count-in-cell and factorial moment analysis
status_evidence.snippet: Ongoing studies of factorial moment scaling and intermittency continue, with comparisons to data still being refined.
status_evidence.claim: The intermittency program remains active, indicating the experimental question is not fully closed.
